subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Which canonical operator-controlled host-root policy should OpenClaw support for image/media tools: shared tools.fs.roots, a narrower media-only root field, or no persistent host-root expansion?
rationale: The requested config changes what model-facing media tools may read from the host, and repository policy treats filesystem boundaries plus config/default surfaces as maintainer/security decisions rather than safe autonomous fixes.

options.title: Use shared filesystem roots
options.body: Adopt a single security-reviewed tools.fs.roots-style contract for filesystem tools and media paths so OpenClaw does not grow competing allowlists.

options.title: Add media-only roots
options.body: Add a narrower media-root config if maintainers want image/PDF/media reads decoupled from read/write/edit filesystem policy, with explicit docs and tests for the split boundary.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Continue requiring copies, symlinks, managed inbound media, or scoped channel attachment roots instead of persistent host-root expansion.

recommendation.title: Use shared filesystem roots
recommendation.body: Adopt a single security-reviewed tools.fs.roots-style contract for filesystem tools and media paths so OpenClaw does not grow competing allowlists.

likelyOwner.reason: The local media root policy and regression coverage history in PR 57770 make this the closest available routing owner for the security-boundary choice.
